w-jp-003.title: Curry Bread (Karee Pan)

instructions.1: Combine the yeast, milk, and sugar in a small bowl, cover, and set aside for 10 minutes, then stir in the egg.
instructions.2: Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Make a well in the center of the flour and add the liquid mixture, stirring to form a soft dough.
instructions.4: Transfer the dough to an electric mixer fitted with a dough hook and knead for about 5 minutes or until smooth and elastic.
instructions.5: With the mixer motor running, add the chopped butter and mix until the butter is combined and a smooth and silky dough forms.
instructions.6: Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and set aside in a warm place to prove for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
instructions.7: Meanwhile, make the curry filling.
instructions.8: Finely chop the carrot, onion, and garlic.
instructions.9: Peel and cut the potato into bite-sized pieces and cook until soft to make mashed potato. Set aside.
instructions.10: Heat olive oil in a frying pan and cook the onion, carrot, and garlic until soft, then add the beef mince and cook.
instructions.11: Add water to the frying pan and bring it to a boil.
instructions.12: Turn the heat down to low and add the Japanese curry roux. Stir and mix until the roux is dissolved.
instructions.13: Add the mashed potato and simmer until the mixture has thickened.
instructions.14: Pour the mixture into a flat container, and when it is set, divide it into 8 even sizes.
instructions.15: Divide the bread dough into 8 equal-sized balls and knead on a lightly floured surface until smooth.
instructions.16: Wrap a piece of the curry filling with a bread roll.
instructions.17: Spray it with olive oil and roll in panko crumbs to coat the bread. Repeat the process for the other 7 pieces.
instructions.18: Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, cover with a clean damp cloth, and set aside for about 45 minutes or until doubled in size.
instructions.19: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and bake for 15 minutes.

w-jp-003.culturalNotes: Curry Bread (Karee Pan) is a popular Japanese pastry, often enjoyed as a snack or part of a breakfast meal.

w-jp-004.title: Daifuku (Sweet Filled Mochi)

instructions.1: Prepare anko filling as directed and shape into 12 small, marble-sized balls. Set aside.
instructions.2: Prepare a smooth surface, such as a cutting board, by coating with potato starch; be generous, as the dough will be very sticky.
instructions.3: Heat water and sugar together in a microwave until sugar is dissolved. Add rice flour and stir completely. Microwave for 2 minutes, remove and stir. Microwave for 2 more minutes, or until dough begins to expand. Remove from microwave, stir again, and remove the dough to the potato starch-coated surface. The dough, called mochi, will be very hot.
instructions.4: Spread or roll the mochi dough out until thin. Using a knife, cut into 12 even sized pieces.
instructions.5: Coat the palms and fingers of your hands in potato starch. Spread each piece out as thin as possible.
instructions.6: Place an anko ball in the middle of each mochi piece, then wrap the mochi around the ball, forming a bigger ball.
instructions.7: Roll shaped daifuku in potato starch, and set on a plate dusted with potato starch or a piece of wax paper.
instructions.8: Serve warm or cool. Store in an airtight container. Very perishable.

w-jp-004.culturalNotes: Daifuku is a traditional Japanese sweet made from sticky rice dough filled with various fillings, such as anko.

w-jp-011.title: Hayashi Rice

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. If you prefer to make the sauce from scratch, you can refer to my Hayashi Rice recipe.
instructions.2: Chop the onions and mushrooms into small pieces.
instructions.3: Heat the butter in a pot over medium heat, then add the onions and mushrooms. Stir until the onions become translucent and the mushrooms are golden.
instructions.4: Add the beef and stir until it is golden brown.
instructions.5: Add the water and bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the Hayashi Rice Sauce (Roux) and stir until it is fully dissolved.
instructions.7: Serve the cooked Japanese short-grain rice with the hot sauce.

w-jp-011.culturalNotes: Hayashi Rice is a traditional Japanese dish that combines Western and Japanese flavors. It is typically served with Japanese short-grain rice.

w-jp-012.title: Imagawayaki (Obanyaki)

w-jp-012-i1.name: eggs
w-jp-012-i1.standardAmount: 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs well, then add the sugar, honey, and milk and mix well.
instructions.3: Add the flour and baking powder and mix until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
instructions.4: Heat the imagawayaki pan over medium heat and grease it with the neutral oil.
instructions.5: Fill each hole in the pan with about 2 tablespoons of batter, then place a small spoonful of sweet red bean paste in the center of each hole.
instructions.6: Cover the filling with batter, then cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown on the bottom.
instructions.7: Flip the imagawayaki and cook for another 3-4 minutes until golden brown on the other side.
instructions.8: Serve the imagawayaki hot or warm.

w-jp-012.culturalNotes: Imagawayaki is a traditional Japanese sweet often served at festivals and special occasions.

w-jp-013.title: Japanese Milk Bread (Shokupan)

w-jp-013-i1.name: bread flour
w-jp-013-i1.standardAmount: 250g + 20g for the yukone and extra for dusting

instructions.1: In a small saucepan, whisk together 20g bread flour with 100ml water until smooth. Put over a low-medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until a thick paste. This happens fast, around 5 mins. Remove from heat and set aside to cool to room temperature.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, or the bowl of a stand mixer, combine 250g bread flour with the yeast, sugar, and salt. Keep the yeast and salt on opposite sides of the bowl so the salt doesn't touch the yeast directly.
instructions.3: Add the cooled yukone, warm milk, and beaten egg. Mix (by hand or with a dough hook) for about 2 mins until it comes together into a rough dough.
instructions.4: Knead the dough until smooth and elastic, around 8 mins in the mixer. Add the softened butter a little at a time and continue kneading for another 8-10 mins until the dough is soft, glossy, and you can stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing.
instructions.5: Shape the dough into a ball, put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp towel, and leave in a warm place to rise until doubled in size, around 1 hr 30 mins.
instructions.6: Punch down the dough and divide into three equal pieces. Roll each piece on a lightly floured surface into an oval, fold the sides in, then roll up from the bottom into a tight cylinder. Put all three pieces seam-side down side by side into an oiled shokupan or 900g loaf tin.
instructions.7: Cover the tin loosely and leave in a warm place until the dough rises to about 80-90 per cent of the tin's height, around 1 hr. If using a lidded shokupan tin, close the lid once it's close to full.
instructions.8: Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. If not using a lidded tin, brush the top of the loaf with the milk or melted butter. Bake for about 20 mins until deep golden brown, then drop the heat to 170C/150C fan/gas 3 and bake for another 5-10 mins until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the base. Turn the loaf out of the tin immediately and cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing. Will keep wrapped for up to three days.

w-jp-013.culturalNotes: Japanese milk bread (shokupan) is a soft, fluffy bread known for its silky texture. It is characterized by its mild sweetness and smooth texture, making it perfect for breakfast or light snacks.

w-jp-014.title: Japanese Glass Noodle Soup

w-jp-014-i1.name: Eggs
w-jp-014-i1.standardAmount: 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

w-jp-014-i8.name: Soy Sauce
w-jp-014-i8.standardAmount: 1½ Tbsp (use gluten-free soy sauce for GF)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Beat 2 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell) in a measuring cup or in a bowl with a spout.
instructions.3: Cut the white part of 2 green onions/scallions into thin round pieces. Then, thinly slice the green part diagonally. Set them aside separately.
instructions.4: Cut 3.5 oz medium-firm tofu (momen dofu) into ½-inch (1.3 cm) cubes.
instructions.5: Add 2 Tbsp dried wakame seaweed to a small bowl of water and rehydrate for 5 minutes. Then, drain and squeeze the water out. Set aside.
instructions.6: Preheat a medium pot over medium heat. When the pot is hot, add 2 tsp roasted sesame oil, then the white part of the green onions.
instructions.7: Stir-fry for 30 seconds until the green onions are well coated with the oil. Then, add 2 cups chicken stock/broth and 2 cups water.
instructions.8: Add 1½ Tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt, and ¼ tsp white pepper powder.
instructions.9: After mixing the soup well, cover the pot with a lid and bring it to a boil.
instructions.10: Once boiling, add the tofu and 1 oz dried glass/cellophane noodles (harusame).
instructions.11: Cook the glass noodles according to the package instructions. Stir the noodles in the beginning so they don’t stick to each other or the bottom of the pot.
instructions.12: After the noodles are cooked, adjust the heat so the soup is simmering (a very gentle boil). Slowly pour a steady trickle of the beaten eggs into the soup in a circular motion, starting from the center and spiraling outward. (Don’t pour on top of any egg that you’ve already added to the soup.) Place cooking chopsticks at the edge of the bowl/measuring cup while pouring so the egg will drizzle down the chopsticks in a thin stream. Let the eggs sit without stirring for 20–25 seconds until they’re fluffy and just cooked.
instructions.13: Add the rehydrated wakame seaweed, green parts of the green onions, and 2 tsp toasted white sesame seeds. Remove the saucepan from the heat to prevent overcooking.
instructions.14: Transfer the glass noodles to individual bowls with a pair of tongs. Then pour the soup and other ingredients over the noodles. Serve hot.

w-jp-014.culturalNotes: Japanese Glass Noodle Soup is a popular dish in Japan, often served as a light meal or part of a lunch.

w-jp-017.title: Japanese Korokke

instructions.1: Peel and dice the potatoes.
instructions.2: Cook the potatoes in boiling water for about 10 minutes.
instructions.3: While the potatoes are cooking, finely chop the onion and carrot and set aside.
instructions.4: Heat olive oil in a frying pan over high heat and add the ground beef to cook.
instructions.5: When the color of most of the ground beef changes, add the onion and carrot and cook for about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
instructions.6: Check if the potatoes are cooked by inserting a skewer. If it goes through, the potatoes are cooked.
instructions.7: Strain the water from the potatoes, put them back in the pot, and shake them around to rough up the outsides a little.
instructions.8: Mash the potatoes with a potato masher while they are warm.
instructions.9: Add the cooked ground beef, onion, and carrot to the mashed potatoes and combine them well.
instructions.10: Divide the mixture into 8 equal-sized flat ovals.
instructions.11: Combine the egg, water, mayonnaise, and flour in a small bowl to make a batter.
instructions.12: Coat each oval with the batter, then place the potato oval into the panko crumbs.
instructions.13: Coat all potato ovals with the panko crumbs.
instructions.14: Heat deep frying oil in a deep pan until it reaches around 180°C (350°F).
instructions.15: Fry each potato oval until crispy and golden brown.
instructions.16: Serve the korokke with salad leaves or any side dish of your choice.

w-jp-017.culturalNotes: Korokke is a popular dish in Japan, consisting of fried croquettes made from mashed potatoes and ground beef.

w-jp-018.title: Kuromitsu (Black Sugar Syrup)

instructions.1: In a small saucepan, mix 3.5 oz of black sugar, ½ cup of granulated sugar (to taste), and ½ cup of water.
instructions.2: Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat. Tip: This kuromitsu is quite rich, so feel free to reduce the amount of granulated sugar or omit it entirely, to your preference.
instructions.3: Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring gently until the sugar dissolves completely and the mixture thickens slightly.
instructions.4: Allow it to cool and transfer to an airtight jar. Keep in the refrigerator for up to a week.

w-jp-018.culturalNotes: Kuromitsu (black sugar syrup) is a rich, sweet liquid used in many traditional Japanese desserts.

w-jp-023.title: Hiroshima Okonomiyaki

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix water, plain flour, and dashi powder until the batter is smooth.
instructions.2: Add a drop of vegetable oil and bonito flakes, and mix well.
instructions.3: Add shredded cabbage, chopped scallions, bean sprouts, tempura crisps, and seaweed flakes, and mix well.
instructions.4: Heat a skillet over medium heat and add olive oil.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the skillet and cook until golden brown on the bottom.
instructions.6: Add the yakisoba noodles and gently mix.
instructions.7: Crack the eggs over the batter and cover the skillet for 2-3 minutes until the eggs are cooked.
instructions.8: Gently flip the batter and cook the other side until done.

w-jp-023.culturalNotes: Hiroshima Okonomiyaki is a popular dish in Japan, especially in Hiroshima. It is known for its thick, rich layers.

w-jp-024.title: Omurice

instructions.1: Cut the chicken, onion, and carrot into small cubes.
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
instructions.3: Add the chicken to the pan and cook until the meat has all turned white.
instructions.4: Add the vegetables and cook until the onion becomes translucent.
instructions.5: Add the ketchup and mix it all together.
instructions.6: Add the rice and mix until the rice is all coated with the ketchup.
instructions.7: Add the thawed frozen peas and mix them with the rice and ketchup.
instructions.8: Flavor with salt and pepper to taste.
instructions.9: Remove from heat and set aside in a large bowl.
instructions.10: In a small bowl, crack and beat 2 eggs.
instructions.11: Heat the large frying pan over medium heat and add 1/2 tbsp of olive oil, then pour in the eggs, allowing them to spread all over the bottom of the pan and slightly scramble the middle without breaking the omelette.
instructions.12: Turn off the heat, and pour half the ketchup rice into the center of the omelette.
instructions.13: Push the omelette and rice to one side of the pan and fold in the sides of the omelette to wrap the rice.
instructions.14: Hold a plate beside the omelette and tip the pan a bit to slide the omelette onto the plate so that it flips onto the plate with the egg on top covering the rice.
instructions.15: Repeat these steps again for the next 2 eggs and remaining chicken rice, then serve!

w-jp-024.culturalNotes: Omurice is a popular Japanese dish that combines rice, chicken, and eggs, often served on family occasions.

w-jp-025.title: Onigiri

instructions.1: Wash the rice and cook it according to the package or rice cooker instructions. Let it cool until it can be handled with your hands.
instructions.2: While the rice is cooking, prepare your fillings.
instructions.3: Fill a bowl with salt water to rinse your fingers and season the onigiri.
instructions.4: Use one of the two methods to shape the onigiri:
instructions.5: Method 1: Wet your hands in the salt water. Take two large spoonfuls of rice into one hand (carefully; the rice is hot), and gently squeeze and flatten it with the other. Make an indentation in the middle, and put some of the filling into the center. Be a little careful to get the filling only in the center and not all over the ball; that can make the rice less sticky, and stickiness is good. 'Fold' the rice over the filling so it becomes covered. Squeeze gently, and mold it into a triangular shape by folding both your hands along the palms while keeping the fingers straight. Squeeze like that, rotating the ball a few times, and you will soon have a very neat triangle—this really is much harder to explain than to do. Once the ball is done, put it down on a clean surface to cool down. Rinse your hands in the salt water and repeat.
instructions.6: Method 2: Use a bowl and some plastic film. Place about ⅔ of the mixture into the center of the cling wrap that has been draped into the bowl loosely. Then, add approximately 2 teaspoons of filling (this is working off of about 3–4 portions per cup of rice). Then, place the last ⅓ of the rice to the top. Then, mold the onigiri within the cling wrap. This drastically reduces mess and also is slightly more 'kid friendly'.
instructions.7: Once the balls are reasonably cool, you need to protect them from drying out. The easiest way is to wrap them in cling wrap, or put them into an airtight plastic food container. When it is time to eat, take one rice ball, wrap it in a piece of nori, and eat away. If you don't mind soggy nori, you can wrap the balls in nori beforehand.

w-jp-025.culturalNotes: Onigiri is a traditional Japanese breakfast dish, often served with various fillings and wrapped in nori sheets.

w-jp-026.title: Cabbage and Onsen Tamago Miso Soup

w-jp-026-i6.name: large eggs
w-jp-026-i6.standardAmount: 3 large eggs (50 g each w/o shell)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. I made 2 onsen tamago (silky poached eggs) today.
instructions.2: Remove the core of ¼ onion and cut into thin slices.
instructions.3: To a medium saucepan, add 3 cups water, the sliced onion, and 2 dashi packets. Cover the saucepan with a lid and bring it to a boil on medium heat.
instructions.4: Remove the core of ⅛ head green cabbage and cut into small, ¾-inch (2-cm) squares. Discard any tough, dense pieces or reserve them for other recipes. Alternatively, you can add them to the saucepan earlier than the leafy parts to give them extra time to cook and soften.
instructions.5: Cut 1 green onion/scallion in half widthwise and diagonally cut into thin slices.
instructions.6: Once the water is boiling, shake the dashi packets with cooking chopsticks to release more flavor. Reduce the heat to medium low and cook, covered, for 4-5 minutes. Then, discard the dashi packets.
instructions.7: Add the cabbage and cook, covered, until both the onion and cabbage are tender, about 4-5 minutes.
instructions.8: To make the onsen tamago: Place the eggs in a bowl of hot water (about 65-70°C) for 12-15 minutes.
instructions.9: Add the miso to the soup and stir well.
instructions.10: Serve the soup hot with the onsen tamago and sliced green onion. You can add shichimi togarashi and Japanese sansho pepper to taste.

w-jp-026.culturalNotes: Onsen tamago is a traditional Japanese dish served in Japanese hot springs. It is slowly cooked in warm water to give it a silky texture.

w-jp-029.title: Japanese Sashimi

instructions.1: Using a very sharp knife, cut the pieces of fish against the grain to about 1/4 inch slices or less.
instructions.2: Arrange the fish on a Japanese tray along with a bunch of shredded daikon radish, some wasabi, and ginger slices.
instructions.3: It is customary to serve with a small dish for the soy sauce, and guests will mix the wasabi with the soy sauce to the desired amount of heat.
instructions.4: The ginger is used to cleanse the palate between different bites.

w-jp-029.culturalNotes: Sashimi is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of carefully sliced raw fish served with complementary ingredients such as wasabi and pickled ginger.

w-jp-030.title: Shiruko (Sweet Red Bean Soup)

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. Make the Shiratama Dango ahead (15 minutes) or toast kirimochi instead.
instructions.2: Add 7 oz of sweet red bean paste (anko) to a saucepan. Pour in half of the water.
instructions.3: Mash the anko with a spatula until no lumps remain.
instructions.4: Pour in the rest of the water and bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Once simmering, cook for 1-2 minutes. Add a pinch of salt (optional).
instructions.5: Serve the sweet red bean soup with the Shiratama Dango.

w-jp-030.culturalNotes: Shiruko is a traditional Japanese dessert usually served in winter. It is known for its sweet taste and creamy texture.

w-jp-035.title: Tamago Kake Gohan

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients. For the steamed rice, ¾ cup (150 g) of uncooked Japanese short-grain rice yields 2¼ US cups (330 g) of cooked white rice.
instructions.2: Add 1 serving of cooked Japanese short-grain rice to a rice bowl. The rice should be steaming hot.
instructions.3: Make a well in the middle of the rice. Crack 1 large egg (50 g without shell) into the well.
instructions.4: Drizzle a small amount of soy sauce onto the egg.
instructions.5: Add toppings of your choice. I like to sprinkle katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes) around the egg in the rice.
instructions.6: Drizzle a bit more soy sauce on the toppings if you wish.
instructions.7: Stir the ingredients with a pair of chopsticks until the egg is fully incorporated into the rice and turns a pale yellow color.
instructions.8: Enjoy!

w-jp-035.culturalNotes: Tamago Kake Gohan is a traditional Japanese breakfast dish often served in the morning. It is known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-jp-036.title: Tamagoyaki

instructions.1: Crack the eggs into a medium-sized mixing bowl.
instructions.2: Add the seasonings (shirodashi and water for dashimaki or sugar, salt, and water for atsumaki) and mix them together gently to avoid too much bubble formation.
instructions.3: Strain the egg mixture through a sieve a few times.
instructions.4: Pour about 2 tbsp of oil into a small bowl and soak kitchen paper and set aside.
instructions.5: Heat 2 tsp of olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat until you can feel the heat when you hover your hand over the pan.
instructions.6: Pour 1/3 of the egg mixture into the pan (you should hear a sizzling sound).
instructions.7: Break any bubbles that have formed with the edge of the chopsticks and scramble gently.
instructions.8: When the surface is solidified a little, fold and push the egg to one end of the pan with chopsticks.
instructions.9: Wipe the empty side of the pan with oil-soaked kitchen paper and pour another 1/3 of the egg mixture into the empty space of the pan.
instructions.10: Lift the folded egg up to let the egg mixture run under it.
instructions.11: Fold and roll the egg from one side of the pan and wipe the empty space of the pan with the oil-soaked kitchen paper.
instructions.12: Pour the last 1/3 of the egg mixture and repeat fold and roll.
instructions.13: Turn the heat off and wrap the rolled egg with a thin kitchen towel.
instructions.14: Roll the wrapped egg roll with a sushi mat to shape and rest to cool down.
instructions.15: Once it is cooled down, slice it 2 cm (0.79 inch) thick and serve.

w-jp-036.culturalNotes: Tamagoyaki is a type of Japanese rolled omelette often served in daily meals.

w-jp-039.title: Buri Teriyaki

instructions.1: Prepare the yellowtail fish fillet. Sprinkle salt and leave it for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: After 15 minutes, wipe the excess liquid off the fish with paper towels.
instructions.3: Heat the butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
instructions.4: Fry the fish on both sides until brown.
instructions.5: Turn up the heat and pour the teriyaki sauce over the fish.
instructions.6: Cook until the sauce has reduced and become thick and shiny.
instructions.7: Turn off the heat and serve the fish with a shiso leaf and radish.

w-jp-039.culturalNotes: Teriyaki is a traditional Japanese dish characterized by its sweet and salty teriyaki sauce.

w-jp-040.title: Tonkatsu Sauce

instructions.1: Gather all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Combine 4½ Tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 2 Tbsp sugar in a jar or small bowl and whisk until the sugar dissolves.
instructions.3: Add 5 Tbsp ketchup and 2 Tbsp oyster sauce and whisk until incorporated.
instructions.4: Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed. The sauce is now ready to use.
instructions.5: For a thicker sauce, refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving.

w-jp-040.culturalNotes: The sauce is typically used with Tonkatsu, a popular dish in Japan.

w-ma-001.title: Lamb Börek

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
instructions.2: Add the garlic and sauté for 1 minute. Add the ground lamb and cook for 5 minutes until browned.
instructions.3: Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, paprika, allspice, cayenne pepper, black pepper, salt, currants, and pine nuts. Stir well.
instructions.4: Add the tomato passata and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: In a small bowl, whisk the egg with the yogurt. Add the egg mixture to the lamb and stir well.
instructions.6: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place a sheet of phyllo pastry on a work surface and brush with melted butter. Repeat with 3 more sheets.
instructions.7: Add the lamb mixture to the top sheet and roll to form tubes. Place the tubes in a buttered baking dish.
instructions.8: Repeat the process until all the sheets and filling are used. Sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired.
instructions.9: Bake the börek for 25-30 minutes until golden and crispy.
instructions.10: To make the yogurt sauce, mix the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt in a bowl. Serve with the börek.

w-ma-001.culturalNotes: Börek is a popular dish in Morocco, also known as lamb börek. It is often served on special occasions.

w-ma-002.title: Baba Ghanoush with Roasted Garlic

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 475F.
instructions.2: Poke holes in the eggplant and rub it with olive oil. Place the eggplant and garlic head on a roasting pan wrapped in foil.
instructions.3: Roast the eggplant, turning occasionally until they collapse. Large eggplant will take 30-45 minutes.
instructions.4: Roast the foil-wrapped garlic for 20 minutes, then remove it from the oven and let it cool.
instructions.5: Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden brown, stirring constantly.
instructions.6: Add half of the pine nuts to a food processor, reserving the other half for garnish. Pop the garlic cloves out of the skins and add them to the processor as well.
instructions.7: Scoop out four cups of eggplant flesh and add it to the processor with lemon juice, tahini, and parsley. Pulse, drizzling in olive oil as needed until the mixture reaches a hummus-like consistency.
instructions.8: Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

w-ma-002.culturalNotes: Baba Ghanoush is a popular dish in Moroccan and Eastern cuisine, served as a dip with Arabic bread.

w-ma-003.title: Moroccan Semolina Pancakes - Beghrir

instructions.1: Combine all ingredients in a blender or food processor and blend on medium to high speed for one minute to achieve a smooth, creamy batter. If you notice anything sticking to the pitcher or bowl, stop to scrape down the sides.
instructions.2: Transfer the batter to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes until the batter appears light and foamy with lots of tiny bubbles.
instructions.3: Heat a nonstick crepe pan over medium heat. When hot, stir the beghrir batter with a ladle, then slowly pour some batter into the center of the pan, allowing it to spread outward on its own.
instructions.4: Cook the pancake without turning until set with no wet spots, about one to two minutes. You can test the pancake by touching it lightly; it should feel spongy and no batter should stick to your finger.
instructions.5: Transfer the pancake to a clean towel to cool. Repeat with the remaining batter, adjusting the heat if necessary to prevent the bottoms of the pancakes from becoming overly brown.
instructions.6: Serve the beghrir dipped in syrup made from melted butter and honey, or with toppings and spreads on the side.

w-ma-003.culturalNotes: Beghrir is a traditional Moroccan breakfast dish, typically served with honey and melted butter.

w-ma-004.title: Bessara

instructions.1: Soak the dried split fava beans in water for at least 12 hours.
instructions.2: Drain and rinse the fava beans thoroughly.
instructions.3: Place the fava beans in a pot with water and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30-40 minutes until tender.
instructions.4: Add the garlic, paprika, cumin, and salt, and stir well.
instructions.5: Use a hand blender or food processor to blend the fava beans until smooth.
instructions.6: Add lemon juice to taste.
instructions.7: Serve hot, garnished with ground cumin, ground cayenne, harissa, and extra virgin olive oil.

w-ma-004.culturalNotes: Bessara is a traditional Moroccan dish served as a soup or dip. It is typically served in a traditional earthenware bowl.

w-ma-007.title: Chebakia

w-ma-007-i9.name: mastic or gum arabic drops
w-ma-007-i9.standardAmount: 1/4 teaspoon, mixed with 1/4 teaspoon sugar and crushed to a powder

instructions.1: Clean and toast the unhulled sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden brown. Let them cool.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, anise, cinnamon, saffron, turmeric, and mastic in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Add the egg, melted butter, olive oil, vinegar, orange flower water, and dissolved yeast. Mix well until the dough is smooth and consistent.
instructions.4: Cover the dough and let it rest for two hours in a warm place.
instructions.5: Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut it into small pieces. Shape each piece into a spiral or flower.
instructions.6: Fry the chebakia in hot vegetable oil until golden brown. Remove and drain on paper towels.
instructions.7: Mix the honey with orange flower water. Dip the chebakia in the warm honey mixture and let it cool.
instructions.8: Garnish the chebakia with toasted sesame seeds and serve.

w-ma-007.culturalNotes: Chebakia is a traditional Moroccan sweet typically served during Ramadan. It is known for its sweet and complex flavor and beautiful shape.

w-ma-008.title: Eggplant Chermoula Salad

w-ma-008-i5.name: white vinegar
w-ma-008-i5.standardAmount: 2 tbsp (or fresh lemon juice to taste)

instructions.1: Cut the eggplants into large cubes.
instructions.2: Soak the eggplants in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain.
instructions.3: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat, add the eggplants and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
instructions.4: Add the chermoula paste, salt, and white vinegar (or fresh lemon juice), and continue to stir for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Transfer the eggplants to a serving dish, and let it cool slightly before serving.

w-ma-008.culturalNotes: Chermoula is a traditional Moroccan marinade used in many dishes, known for its rich and spicy flavor.

w-ma-011.title: Moroccan Semolina Cookies with Anise, Raisins and Sesame - Baked Harcha

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 170°C (338°F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, mix the fine semolina, all-purpose flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, sesame seeds, anise seeds, and raisins.
instructions.3: Add the vanilla, eggs, melted butter, and milk. Mix well until the dough is smooth.
instructions.4: Shape the dough into small balls and place them on the baking sheets. Press each ball with a spoon to flatten it.
instructions.5: Sprinkle each ball with coarse or fine semolina and sugar.
instructions.6: Bake the cookies in the oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.7: Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.

w-ma-011.culturalNotes: Moroccan harcha is a traditional type of cookie often served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ma-012.title: Moroccan Harira Soup

w-ma-012-i17.name: tomato paste (combined with 1 or 2 cups water)

w-ma-012-i20.name: lemon wedges and cilantro (optional) for garnish

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas and lentils in water for at least 8 hours or overnight.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the meat and stir until golden brown.
instructions.3: Add the bones (if using), tomatoes, chickpeas, lentils, onion, celery, parsley, cilantro, smen (if using), salt, ginger, black pepper, cinnamon (if using), and turmeric. Mix the ingredients well.
instructions.4: Add enough water to cover the ingredients. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for an hour and a half or until the chickpeas and lentils are tender.
instructions.5: Add the tomato paste mixed with water, rice or broken vermicelli, and flour mixed with water. Stir well and bring the soup to a boil again for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Serve the harira hot, garnished with lemon wedges and cilantro if desired.

w-ma-012.culturalNotes: Harira is a traditional Moroccan soup often served during Ramadan. It is an ideal breakfast meal to start the day.

w-ma-015.title: Makroudh

instructions.1: In a food processor with the dough blade attached, mix the flour, salt, and olive oil together, scraping the sides once or twice.
instructions.2: Once all the grains are coated with oil, drizzle in the warm water until the mixture begins to pull together into a ball. Some of it will be moist, and a little bit will be dry.
instructions.3: Remove it all and knead together for a few minutes until a smooth ball forms. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Cut pieces of the dough and roll them into snakes, then cut the snakes into 1.5-inch pieces. Press each piece with a fork to make little indentations.
instructions.5: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the makroudh for 10-15 minutes, depending on the thickness.
instructions.6: After cooking, drain the makroudh and coat it with a few spoonfuls of toum (lemon garlic sauce).

w-ma-015.culturalNotes: Makroudh is a traditional Moroccan dish often served on special occasions.

w-ma-016.title: M'rouzia

instructions.1: Mix the lamb with Ras-el-hanout and ground pepper. Let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the lamb and brown on all sides.
instructions.3: Add the chopped onion, ginger, smen, salt, cinnamon stick, and saffron. Cook for 5 minutes until the onion is golden.
instructions.4: Add enough water to cover the lamb. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for an hour and a half until the lamb is tender.
instructions.5: Add the raisins, Ras el Hanout, cinnamon, and honey. Cook for 15 minutes until the raisins are soft.
instructions.6: In a separate pan, fry the almonds until golden. Set aside.
instructions.7: Serve the M'rouzia hot, garnished with the fried almonds.

w-ma-016.culturalNotes: M'rouzia is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ma-017.title: Moroccan Msemen

w-ma-017-i8.name: fine semolina
w-ma-017-i8.standardAmount: 1/2 cup (can use coarser caliber if you like)

instructions.1: Mix the flour, semolina, sugar, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Gradually add the warm water and knead the ingredients until the dough becomes smooth and elastic.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into small balls.
instructions.5: Roll out each ball using a fork or your fingers until it is very thin.
instructions.6: Heat a skillet over medium heat and add a little oil.
instructions.7: Place the flattened dough in the skillet and fry it on both sides until golden brown.
instructions.8: Repeat the process with the remaining dough balls.
instructions.9: Serve the msemen hot with butter and fine semolina.

w-ma-017.culturalNotes: Msemen is a traditional Moroccan dish usually served with tea or as a breakfast meal.

w-ma-018.title: Moroccan Pastilla

w-ma-018-i17.name: salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a large frying pan.
instructions.2: Add the chicken and fry until golden brown.
instructions.3: Turn the thighs over and cook for a few more minutes, then remove them from the pan.
instructions.4: Add the butter to the pan and when it has melted, add the onions and fry over low heat until soft.
instructions.5: Add the garlic and spices and fry for a few more minutes.
instructions.6: Return the chicken to the pan and add the stock.
instructions.7: Season, then cover the pan and simmer for about half an hour or until the chicken is tender. Remove the chicken and set it aside.
instructions.8: When the chicken is cool enough to handle, finely chop the meat.
instructions.9: Return the liquid to the heat and reduce it by half.
instructions.10: Add the eggs to the liquid and continue to cook over low heat until you have a mixture that resembles loose scrambled eggs.
instructions.11: Add the ground almonds and stir, then add the dates, orange blossom water, zest, and finally, the chicken.
instructions.12: Remove the pan from the heat and allow to cool.
instructions.13: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
instructions.14: To assemble the pastilla, use a 9-inch pie plate or tin.
instructions.15: Take a sheet of filo pastry and brush it with melted butter. Place it in the dish, gently pushing it into the edges without tearing.
instructions.16: Repeat with another sheet of filo, this time placing it at a right angle to the first.
instructions.17: Repeat with two more sheets of filo, this time placing them on the diagonal.
instructions.18: Spread the filling over the pastry. Fold over the overhanging pieces of filo in reverse order – they should just about cover the filling.
instructions.19: Take the remaining two pieces of filo and cut them to fit the dish.
instructions.20: Brush them with butter, then cover the pastilla, tucking under any edges.
instructions.21: Bake in the oven for about 30 minutes until the pastry is a crisp, golden brown.
instructions.22: Remove from the oven and allow to cool a little before dusting it with powdered sugar and cinnamon.

w-ma-018.culturalNotes: Pastilla is a traditional Moroccan dish that combines sweet and savory flavors, often served on special occasions.

w-ma-019.title: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into pieces. Place it in a bowl and sprinkle with salt, saffron, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, smen, chopped coriander, and parsley. Mix well and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the oil and sauté the onions until golden brown. Add the garlic, turmeric, and salt, and stir for a minute.
instructions.3: Add the chicken pieces to the pot and stir until they turn golden. Add water to cover the chicken and bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the chicken livers (if using), preserved lemon, and olives. Mix well and let it cook for an additional 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve the chicken hot with rice or Moroccan bread.

w-ma-019.culturalNotes: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives is a traditional dish in Moroccan cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-ma-020.title: Meknes Style Rfissa

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into small pieces.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onions until golden brown.
instructions.3: Add the spices (ras el hanout, black pepper, ginger, turmeric, salt, cayenne pepper, saffron) and stir for a minute.
instructions.4: Add the chicken and stir until it is coated with the spices.
instructions.5: Add the tomatoes, garlic, parsley, cilantro, za'atar, fliou, merseta, fenugreek seeds, lentils (if using), and smen (if available).
instructions.6: Add water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
instructions.7: Reduce the heat and simmer for an hour and a half until the chicken is cooked.
instructions.8: Add the shredded msemen and simmer for another 15 minutes.
instructions.9: Serve the rfissa hot, garnished with ground fried almonds, dates, and hard-boiled eggs.

w-ma-020.culturalNotes: Rfissa is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions, such as holidays and family gatherings.

w-ma-023.title: Shakshouka

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the red bell peppers, Anaheim peppers, onion, and garlic. Brown the vegetables for 15-30 minutes until they are soft and browned.
instructions.2: Add the tomatoes (without the juice) and crush them with a wooden spoon. Reserve the juice for thinning the sauce later if desired. Cover and simmer gently for an hour.
instructions.3: Before serving, break the eggs on top of the gently simmering sauce. Cover the skillet and poach the eggs for 3-5 minutes until they are cooked to your desired doneness.
instructions.4: Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve the dish in the pot it was cooked in.

w-ma-023.culturalNotes: Shakshouka is a popular dish in Morocco and North African countries, typically served as a breakfast or light lunch.

w-ma-024.title: Moroccan Tagine (Lamb with Prunes and Apricots)

w-ma-024-i9.name: lamb
w-ma-024-i9.standardAmount: 1 lb (from shoulder, leg, or shanks, cubed)

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a tagine, add the almonds and cook until golden.
instructions.2: Add the onions and garlic and sauté until translucent.
instructions.3: Add the ginger, saffron, cinnamon sticks, and coriander seeds, and stir well.
instructions.4: Add the lamb and coat it well, sauté for a minute or two.
instructions.5: Pour in enough water to cover the meat and bring it to a boil.
instructions.6: Reduce the heat, cover the tagine, and let it cook for about an hour.
instructions.7: Add the prunes, apricots, and orange peel, and simmer for 20 more minutes covered.
instructions.8: Add salt and pepper to taste.
instructions.9: Stir in the honey and half of the chopped cilantro leaves, and add a little water if necessary.
instructions.11: Adjust the seasoning as necessary, garnish with cilantro, and serve.

w-ma-024.culturalNotes: Tagine is a traditional Moroccan dish cooked in a special pot called a tagine. It is usually served with couscous or bread.

w-ma-029.title: Kebab Maghdour

w-ma-029-i15.name: Eggs
w-ma-029-i15.standardAmount: 3-6 (counting half to a whole egg per person)

w-ma-029-i17.name: Chopped flat leaf parsley or coriander

instructions.1: Prepare the meat by cutting it into 1-inch cubes.
instructions.2: In a bowl, mix the meat with grated onion, garlic, ginger, pepper, parsley and coriander, and vegetable oil. Let the mixture marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: In a pot, add the vegetable and olive oil, then add the finely chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
instructions.4: Add the marinated meat to the pot and sauté for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Add water to cover the meat, then add ginger, salt, cinnamon stick, and ground sweet paprika. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
instructions.6: Add the eggs to the pot and cook for 10 minutes until they are done.
instructions.7: Serve the Kebab Maghdour hot, garnished with chopped parsley.

w-ma-029.culturalNotes: Kebab Maghdour is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions. It is known for its rich spice flavors and tender meat.

w-mx-003.title: Alfajor (Hispanoamérica)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cornstarch, and orange zest.
instructions.3: In another bowl, beat egg yolks until pale yellow.
instructions.4: Add dry ingredients to egg yolks in three parts, mixing the orange juice in between. If the dough seems sticky, add extra cornstarch one tablespoon at a time, until the dough comes together and is no longer sticky.
instructions.5: Roll the dough out thinly (about 3 mm). Only roll one side of the dough or else it won’t curl when baked.
instructions.6: Cut out the shapes and prick with a fork so they won't puff up.
instructions.7: Bake for 4-7 minutes. Do not let them brown. They should remain soft and tender. Let cool.
instructions.8: Spread with dulce de leche. Put two halves together and enjoy. Dust with powdered sugar if desired.

w-mx-003.culturalNotes: Alfajor is a popular dessert in Latin America, especially in Argentina and Peru. It is often served at special occasions and celebrations.

w-mx-004.title: Arroz Poblano

instructions.1: Place the rice in a bowl with warm water and set aside for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, place the chopped onion, garlic clove, and 1/2 cup of cold water in a blender and process until you have a smooth mixture.
instructions.3: After 15 minutes, drain the water and rinse the rice with cold water until the water is clear. Make sure to drain well and shake off any excess water; it has to be as dry as possible.
instructions.4: Add vegetable oil to a saucepan or cazuela and place over medium-high heat. Heat the oil and add the rice. Fry the rice, stirring constantly until it becomes transparent, about 12 minutes. Use a spoon to drain any excess oil after this step.
instructions.5: Add the onion and garlic mixture to the rice and stir (be careful not to break the rice grains).
instructions.6: Add the hot water, parsley sprigs, and Serrano pepper (if using) and a few drops of lime juice.
instructions.7: When the water starts boiling, lower the heat to the lowest temperature, season with salt to taste, and cover the saucepan. Do not remove the lid.
instructions.8: After 20 minutes, the water should be absorbed almost completely. The rice should look cooked and soft. Remove from heat and let stand for about 10 minutes. Discard the parsley sprig and serve. The rice will continue to cook with its own heat.

w-mx-004.culturalNotes: Arroz Poblano is a traditional Mexican dish, known for its rich and subtle flavor.

w-mx-009.title: Caldo Tlalpeño

w-mx-009-i9.name: carrots
w-mx-009-i9.standardAmount: 2 carrots, peeled and sliced into half-moons

instructions.1: Add the chicken thighs, water, onion, garlic, salt, and bay leaves to a large pot or Dutch oven. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
instructions.2: Transfer the chicken to a bowl to cool, discard the bay leaves, and transfer the cooked onions and garlic into a blender. Strain and reserve the remaining broth in a large bowl.
instructions.3: In the blender with the cooked onions and garlic, add 1 cup of the reserved chicken broth, the tomatoes, salt, and chipotle pepper in adobo sauce. Blend until smooth.
instructions.4: Heat the olive oil in the same large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the carrots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften. Add the diced onion and cook for 5 more minutes until softened and translucent.
instructions.5: Pour in the blended tomato mixture and cook for an additional 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.6: While the tomato mixture cooks, shred the chicken thighs.
instructions.7: Add the shredded chicken, green beans, chickpeas, remaining chicken broth, epazote leaves, and cilantro sprigs to the pot. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Cook for 8 minutes until the green beans are tender. Taste and season with more salt if needed.
instructions.8: Serve immediately in bowls and garnish with a chipotle pepper in adobo sauce, crumbled queso fresco, sliced avocados, and chopped cilantro.

w-mx-009.culturalNotes: Caldo Tlalpeño is a traditional Mexican soup, often served in a traditional clay bowl.

w-mx-010.title: Capirotada (Mexican Bread Pudding)

w-mx-010-i6.name: shredded cheese (Longhorn Cheddar, Colby, or cheese of your choice)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
instructions.2: Cut the rolls into 1/2 inch slices and butter both sides, then place them on a baking sheet and bake for 3 minutes on each side until lightly toasted and dry. Remove and let cool.
instructions.3: Combine the water, piloncillo, cinnamon sticks, and cloves in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove from heat and let steep, covered, for 2 hours. Strain the liquid and discard the cinnamon sticks and cloves.
instructions.4: Spray an 8 x 10 1/2” baking dish with non-stick spray, then layer the ingredients in the following order: a third of the toasted bread, a third of the raisins, a third of the cheese, and 1 1/2 cups of the syrup. Wait 15 minutes, then layer another third of the bread, raisins, cheese, and syrup. Let it soak for another 15 minutes, and again top with the remaining bread, raisins, cheese, and syrup. Let it set for another 15 minutes before baking.
instructions.5: Cover the dish with aluminum foil that has been sprayed with non-stick spray and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake until the cheese is golden brown, about 10 to 15 minutes more. Serve warm.

w-mx-010.culturalNotes: Capirotada is a traditional Mexican dessert served during Lent. It is known for its sweet and savory flavor and its crunchy and moist texture.

w-mx-011.title: Carne a la Tampiqueña

instructions.1: In a large frying pan over medium-low heat, melt the butter. When the butter foams, add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until translucent and starting to brown lightly, 12-14 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the chile strips and cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes to mix well. Remove from the heat and set aside.
instructions.3: Prepare a fire in a charcoal or gas grill for direct grilling over medium-high heat. Preheat the broiler.
instructions.4: Season the steak on both sides with salt and pepper and cut into 4 equal servings. Line a sheet pan with aluminum foil.
instructions.5: Place the steak on the grill, close the lid, and grill, turning once, for 2-3 minutes on each side for medium-rare to medium, or cook to your desired doneness.
instructions.6: Transfer the steak to the foil-lined sheet pan and let rest for 2 minutes. If you want to serve the steak a la mexicana, transfer the steak to a cutting board, chop it, and then return it to the sheet pan.
instructions.7: Top the steak with the onion and chile mixture and sprinkle with the cheese. Place under the broiler and broil until the cheese melts and bubbles, 1-2 minutes. Serve at once.

w-mx-011.culturalNotes: Carne a la Tampiqueña is a famous dish in Mexico, particularly in the state of Tampico, where it is often served on special occasions.

w-mx-012.title: Cemita Buns (Mexican Sesame Bread)

instructions.1: Pour the warm water into a small heat-proof bowl and microwave on high for 20 seconds, or until it reaches 110-115°F. Stir in the yeast and 1 tablespoon of the sugar, then cover with plastic wrap and let it bloom for 10 minutes, until it's foamy and frothy.
instructions.2: In the bowl of a stand mixer or a large bowl, whisk together the flour, the remaining 2 tablespoons of granulated sugar, and the salt.
instructions.3: Add the yeast mixture, the melted butter, and the egg. Using the dough hook attachment (or your hands), knead the dough on medium speed for 8-10 minutes, until it forms a smooth, slightly tacky but not sticky dough ball.
instructions.4: Transfer the dough to a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel, and let it rest in a warm place until it doubles in size, about 1½ to 2 hours.
instructions.5: Punch down the dough and transfer it to a floured surface. Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
instructions.6: Place a dough ball on the work surface. Rest the pinky side of your hand across it, about a third of the way in from one edge, and roll back and forth to squeeze that section thinner. You'll end up with a small ball on top of a bigger ball, joined by a short neck, like a snowman.
instructions.7: Press the whole thing flat with your palm, keeping the snowman shape. The bottom should be about 5 inches across and the top a little smaller.
instructions.8: Pick up the small end, twist it a half turn so it flips over, and lay it down on top of the bigger end. Press the whole bun flat again to about 5½ to 6 inches, pinching the edges so the seams seal. You'll see a curved ridge across the top where the two pieces meet. Repeat with the rest.
instructions.9: Transfer the shaped buns onto the prepared baking sheet. Cover with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and allow them to rise in a warm place until almost doubled in size, about 1 to 1½ hours. During the last 20 minutes of rising, preheat the oven to 350°F.
instructions.10: Whisk together the egg yolk and 2 teaspoons of water until combined. Brush the egg wash over the tops of the buns, then sprinkle generously with sesame seeds.

w-mx-012.culturalNotes: Cemita poblana is a traditional bread from the state of Puebla in Mexico, commonly used for making sandwiches.

w-mx-019.title: Chochoyotes (Bolita de Masa)

w-mx-019-i10.name: carrot
w-mx-019-i10.standardAmount: 1 large carrot (peeled and diced into 1/2-inch pieces)

instructions.1: Mix the masa harina and salt in a large bowl until combined. Pour in the warm water and mix with a fork or your hands until a dough forms and is no longer sticky.
instructions.2: Divide the dough into 16 small portions, then roll each into a ball. Using your thumb, press gently in the middle of each ball to create a small indentation. Cover the chochoyotes with a damp paper towel or kitchen towel while you prepare the vegetable soup.
instructions.3: In a large blender, add the tomatoes, onion, garlic, vegetable bouillon, and water. Blend until smooth.
instructions.4: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the carrots and sauté for 2-3 minutes until they start to soften. Pour in the blended tomato mixture and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the broth, zucchini, corn, cumin, oregano, salt, and black pepper. Bring everything to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Gently drop the prepared chochoyotes into the pot and top with cilantro sprigs. Cover and cook for an additional 15 minutes until the vegetables and chochoyotes are tender and cooked through.
instructions.6: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve in bowls and garnish with lime juice, queso fresco, and sliced avocados.

w-mx-019.culturalNotes: Chochoyotes are a traditional Mexican dish typically served with soup or broth. They are known for their smooth texture and chewy consistency.

w-mx-020.title: Churro

instructions.1: Sift the flour, baking soda, and salt into a large mixing bowl.
instructions.2: Add the boiling water gradually to the flour, mixing constantly until you get a very thick, smooth paste.
instructions.3: Allow to stand for about an hour.
instructions.4: Heat up a deep frying pan of oil until it shimmers.
instructions.5: Using an icing bag or a freezer bag with the corner cut out to give a hole about the size of your little finger, squeeze the paste into the pan. Use a pair of scissors to cut the sausage-shaped pieces off after about 10 cm.
instructions.6: Fry the churros until golden brown and crunchy. If the pieces are too thick and are still raw in the middle, cut them in half lengthwise and fry again.
instructions.7: Remove churros from oil, and drain on a rack or paper towels.
instructions.8: Serve dusted liberally with sugar or hot chocolate sauce (or both).

w-mx-020.culturalNotes: Churros are a popular sweet in Mexico and are often enjoyed with hot chocolate in the morning or as a snack.

w-mx-021.title: Clemole de Pollo

instructions.1: Break open the chiles and remove the seeds and veins.
instructions.2: Place the chiles in a pan and cover with water.
instructions.3: Bring the water to a boil and then turn off the heat and let the chiles reconstitute for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the whole tomatoes to a pot and cover them with water.
instructions.5: Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
instructions.6: Blend the tomatoes and chiles with a little bit of the water you used to soak the chiles to form a loose paste.
instructions.7: Set aside the chile tomato base.
instructions.8: Put the chicken in the pot with 8 cups of water, the whole onion, and the head of garlic. Cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
instructions.9: Add the chunks of corn, chayote, and epazote. Cook for 15 more minutes over low heat.
instructions.10: Add the chunks of zucchini squash and green beans.
instructions.11: Strain the blended guajillo chile tomato base directly into the pot.
instructions.12: Bring to a boil and remove any foam that rises to the top.
instructions.13: Reduce the heat and cook for 20 minutes.
instructions.14: Add 1 tsp of salt. Then add as much salt as needed to your taste.
instructions.15: Discard the onion, epazote, and head of garlic before serving.

w-mx-021.culturalNotes: Clemole de Pollo is a traditional Mexican dish served on special occasions.

w-mx-022.title: Cocada (Dulce)

instructions.1: In a large pot over medium heat, cook water, sugar, and cloves. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Heat until the mixture reaches the soft-ball stage on a candy thermometer (about 240F).
instructions.2: Using a spoon, carefully discard the cloves.
instructions.3: Add shredded coconut and milk. The mixture will clump. Continue to stir until smooth. Simmer for a few minutes.
instructions.4: Spoon into serving dishes and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

w-mx-022.culturalNotes: Cocada is a traditional Mexican dessert, typically made from coconut and sugar.

w-mx-025.title: Enfrijoladas

instructions.1: Add the canned beans, chipotle peppers, onions, garlic, vegetable stock, salt, and oregano into a large blender. Blend until the black bean sauce is silky smooth.
instructions.2: Heat a medium pot or skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon of oil and pour in the bean sauce. Cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture is hot and bubbly, about 5 minutes. If the sauce gets too thick, add some water or broth and mix it in.
instructions.3: To fry (optional): Fill a large sauté pan or deep skillet with about ½ inch of oil and heat over medium-high heat until the temperature reaches 350°F. Test the oil by dropping a small piece of tortilla in it. If it sizzles, it's ready. Fry the tortillas one at a time for about 15 seconds. Transfer them to a large plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels to soak up any excess oil. Continue frying the remaining tortillas.
instructions.4: If not frying, heat up the corn tortillas in a skillet or in the microwave for 1 minute until warm and pliable.
instructions.5: To assemble the enfrijoladas, dip each tortilla into the bean sauce. Transfer the tortilla to a plate and fill with queso fresco. Roll it up like an enchilada, or fold it over like a taco.
instructions.6: Serve immediately topped with sliced red onions, fresh cilantro, and Mexican crema.

w-mx-025.culturalNotes: Enfrijoladas are a traditional Mexican dish often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-mx-026.title: Entomatada

w-mx-026-i14.name: crumbled cotija or more queso fresco

instructions.1: Add the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, garlic, salt, cumin, Mexican oregano, and broth to a blender. Blend until completely smooth.
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the blended tomato mixture and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 6-8 minutes until slightly thickened. Cover and set aside.
instructions.3: Heat the vegetable oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Working one tortilla at a time, lightly fry each tortilla for about 15-30 seconds per side. Drain off any excess oil by giving it a little shake while holding it with tongs, then transfer it onto a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
instructions.4: Assemble the entomatadas by dipping each tortilla in the blended tomato mixture, then placing it on a plate, filling it with queso fresco, and folding it over.
instructions.5: Top with a few more spoonfuls of the blended tomato mixture, then garnish with more queso fresco, Mexican crema, and chopped cilantro.

w-mx-026.culturalNotes: Entomatada is a traditional Mexican dish often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-mx-031.title: Pineapple Horchata

instructions.1: Peel the pineapple and remove the core, then add the pieces to a large pot.
instructions.2: Add the rice and water to the pot, mix the ingredients, and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Meanwhile, chop the remaining pineapple into bite-sized pieces (reserve some for garnish).
instructions.4: After simmering, blend the rice water with up to 2 cups of cubed pineapple. Use an immersion blender or a regular blender (make sure to cool it before blending).
instructions.5: Strain the horchata and whisk it with sugar to taste.
instructions.6: You can drink the horchata straight, which will have a smoothie consistency, or dilute it with water to make it thinner. Serve with a spear of sweet pineapple or several cubes.

w-mx-031.culturalNotes: Horchata is a traditional Mexican drink served cold on hot days.

w-mx-032.title: Huarache (food)

w-mx-032-i2.name: beef chuck steak
w-mx-032-i2.standardAmount: 1 ½ pound (diced into small bite-sized cubes)

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the steak, onion, garlic, salt, and black pepper and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat is no longer pink. Remove from heat and cover until ready to serve.
instructions.2: Combine the masa harina and salt in a large bowl. Stir in the water until a dough forms. Knead the dough with your hands until it fully comes together and all the water is absorbed. To make sure it’s ready, grab a small piece and roll it into a ball. Press down on it with a finger. If the edges of the dough crack, the dough is too dry. If the dough sticks to your skin, it’s too wet. Add more water or masa harina as necessary.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions, then roll each portion into balls and cover them with a clean damp cloth or plastic wrap to keep the dough moist while you press and cook the huaraches.
instructions.4: Heat a griddle or large skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
instructions.5: Shape each dough portion into a 5 to 6-inch log. Working one at a time, place the dough between two sheets of parchment paper or plastic wrap and flatten gently with a tortilla press, a heavy glass baking dish, or the palm of your hand until it’s about ¼-inch thick. Using your hands, shape the flattened dough into an oblong shape so that it looks like the outline of a sandal. Carefully peel the plastic wrap or parchment paper back and transfer the huarache to your hand.
instructions.6: Cook: Cooking 1 or 2 at a time, place the huarache on the hot griddle and cook for 1 minute, or until light brown spots appear on the bottom. Flip and cook the other side for 1 more minute. You can eat the huaraches like this or continue to fry them for a crispier and more delicious dish.
instructions.7: Fry (optional): Fill a large sauté pan or deep skillet with about 1 inch of oil and heat over medium-high heat until the temperature reaches 350°F. (To test, drop a small piece of dough in the oil. If it sizzles, it's ready.) Cooking in batches, carefully add 1 or 2 huaraches into the frying oil and fry for about 1 minute per side until golden brown. Transfer them to a large plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels to soak up any excess oil.
instructions.8: Assemble and serve: Spread a spoonful of warm refried beans onto each huarache, then top with the cooked meat. Drizzle with salsa roja or your favorite hot sauce, salsa verde or guacamole salsa, diced avocados, and crumbled cotija cheese or queso fresco.

w-mx-032.culturalNotes: Huarache is a traditional Mexican dish, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-mx-033.title: Huevos Rancheros

instructions.1: Roughly chop the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and serrano chile.
instructions.2: Add the ingredients to a blender jar with thyme and 2 tablespoons of water.
instructions.3: Blend until smooth for about 1 minute.
instructions.4: Heat 1 tablespoon of cooking oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
instructions.5: Carefully pour the contents of the blender into the saucepan with the hot oil and simmer for about 10 minutes until the salsa is deep red and has thickened slightly.
instructions.6: Season with salt to taste.
instructions.7: Pour 1/2 cup of cooking oil into a medium-sized frying pan and heat the oil over medium heat.
instructions.8: Fry the tortillas for about 20 seconds on each side, being careful not to let them harden.
instructions.9: Drain the tortillas on paper towels and set aside.
instructions.10: Use the same cooking oil to fry the eggs over medium heat.
instructions.11: Add two eggs to the hot oil and slightly tilt the pan so that the eggs set closely together.
instructions.12: Cook until the whites are just set and the yolks are still runny.
instructions.13: Place 2 tortillas on a serving plate and add a good-sized spoonful of refried beans.
instructions.14: Gently place the eggs on the tortillas.
instructions.15: Spoon the warm spicy tomato salsa over the eggs.
instructions.16: Garnish the beans with 3 tortilla chips.

w-mx-033.culturalNotes: Huevos Rancheros is a traditional Mexican breakfast dish, often served in family breakfasts.

w-mx-034.title: Machacado con Huevo

instructions.1: Heat the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
instructions.2: Add the eggs; cook, stirring frequently, for 2-3 minutes or until the eggs just begin to set.
instructions.3: Stir in the shredded beef. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 2-3 minutes or until the eggs are cooked and the beef is heated through.
instructions.4: Serve the eggs with tortillas, refried beans, cheese, and salsa.

w-mx-034.culturalNotes: Machacado con Huevo is a traditional Mexican dish, typically served as a breakfast or light lunch.

w-mx-035.title: Mexican Green Rice

instructions.1: Add cilantro, onion, garlic, and 1/2 cup of water to a blender and blend until smooth for about 1 minute.
instructions.2: Preheat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pot over medium heat.
instructions.3: Add the uncooked rice to the hot oil and stir for about 30 seconds until the rice starts to brown and becomes fragrant.
instructions.4: Add the cilantro mixture to the rice.
instructions.5: Add 4 cups of water and 1 teaspoon of salt to the rice and stir once to evenly disperse the cilantro mixture.
instructions.6: Reduce the heat to low (do not cover) and cook the rice for about 20 minutes until it has completely absorbed the liquid.
instructions.7: If the rice isn't fully cooked after it has absorbed the liquid, add 1/4 cup of water as needed until the rice is fully cooked and the water has been absorbed.
instructions.8: Once the rice is done cooking, turn off the heat and fluff the rice with a fork. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
instructions.9: Garnish with a sprig of cilantro before serving.

w-mx-035.culturalNotes: Mexican green rice is a popular side dish in Mexican cuisine, often served with a variety of main dishes.

w-mx-036.title: Mole de Olla

w-mx-036-i15.name: carrot
w-mx-036-i15.standardAmount: 3 small or 1 large (cut into large pieces)

instructions.1: Rinse the meat and pat dry thoroughly with a paper towel. In a large stockpot, place the meat, onion, garlic, and bay leaves. Cover with 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce heat to simmer gently. Use a slotted spoon to remove any foam that rises to the surface. The meat will take about 1 ½ to 2 hours to cook.
instructions.2: While the meat is cooking, prepare the sauce. Fill a small pot with 2 cups of hot water and set aside. I like roasting the ingredients of the salsa since it gives a rustic flavor to the soup. Now, slightly roast the peppers in a hot griddle, turning once. Remember, this step takes only a few seconds if you leave the peppers longer on the hot griddle they will have a bitter taste. Place the roasted peppers in the pot with the hot water to soften them, at least 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Roast the tomato, garlic, and onion on the hot griddle. The garlic will take less time to roast, so remove promptly. Remove its peel and place in your blender pitcher. Once the tomato and onion are roasted, place them into the blender as well. Once the peppers have softened, add them into the blender along with a cup of the soaking water. Proceed to puree until you have a very smooth sauce. Set aside.
instructions.4: To cook the vegetables: In another medium size saucepan, add 3 cups of water and the pieces of corn to cook over medium-high heat. 8-10 minutes later, add the xoconostle, chayote, and carrots. About 3 minutes after that, add the potatoes (if using) and finally the squash and green beans to cook for 4 more minutes. Don’t worry if they still look uncooked after this time, they will finish cooking with the meat and sauce.
instructions.5: Check your meat. If it is already cooked and tender, remove the garlic, onion, and bay leaf. Now, add the sauce and the Epazote sprigs, stir, and keep simmering for about 8 more minutes. Add the vegetables and stir well. Let it simmer for another 6 minutes to allow all the flavors to blend. You can pour it using a strainer if you want, personally, I don’t use a strainer with this soup since I like how the sauce gives the soup a thicker texture.
instructions.6: To serve, ladle the soup in large bowls with some portions of meat, corn, carrots, chayote, xoconostle, squash, potato, and green beans. Garnish with chopped onion, cilantro, epazote, and lime juice.
instructions.7: Serve with some warm corn tortillas. There you have it, a whole meal in a bowl!

w-mx-036.culturalNotes: Mole de Olla is a traditional Mexican soup rich in flavors, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-mx-041.title: Pastel Azteca

instructions.1: Make the salsa verde: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the tomatillos, onion, jalapeños, and garlic. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.2: Transfer all the ingredients to a blender, and pour in the broth, salt, and lime juice. Blend until smooth and set aside.
instructions.3: Make the chicken and corn filling: Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Add the corn, onion, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin, and black pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, until the onions begin to soften. Remove from the heat and add the shredded chicken and the blended salsa verde. Mix together to combine and set aside to cool slightly.
instructions.4: Roast the poblano peppers: While the chicken and corn mixture is cooling, arrange the poblano peppers on a baking sheet and broil them for about 5 minutes on each side until the skin is blackened and charred.
instructions.5: Cover the baking sheet with aluminum foil to trap the heat and allow the skin to soften for about 5 minutes.
instructions.6: Peel off the charred skin using a butter knife or your hands, getting as much off as you can. Make a vertical slit down the middle and scoop out the seeds. Slice the roasted poblanos into strips and set aside.
instructions.7: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
instructions.8: Prepare the tortillas: Heat the remaining 1/3 cup of olive oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Working one tortilla at a time, lightly fry each tortilla for about 10-15 seconds per side. Drain off any excess oil by giving it a little shake while holding it with tongs, then transfer it onto a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels. Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
instructions.9: Mix the cheese: In a large bowl, combine the shredded cheeses.
instructions.10: Assemble: In a 9x13 inch baking dish, add a layer of tortillas by placing 3 down the middle in a single layer without overlapping, and then 2 on each long end so half of it overlaps with the tortillas in the middle and half fold up along the edge of the baking dish. Spread ¼ cup of Mexican crema on top, then add ⅓ of the chicken and corn mixture, ⅓ of the roasted poblano strips, and ⅓ of the shredded cheese. Repeat this process with 2 additional layers.

w-mx-041.culturalNotes: Pastel Azteca is a traditional Mexican dish that combines layers of tortillas, fillings, and cheese, making it a rich and flavorful dish.

w-mx-042.title: Mexican Picadillo

instructions.1: Peel the carrots and potatoes.
instructions.2: Chop the potatoes and carrots into small pieces.
instructions.3: Preheat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
instructions.4: Add the ground beef to the frying pan and brown it (about 5 minutes).
instructions.5: Add the potatoes and carrots, stir and cook for 6 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the raisins and peas and stir.
instructions.7: Add the tomato sauce, salt, and black pepper and stir.
instructions.8: Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 20 minutes until the liquid has reduced and the potatoes and carrots have softened.
instructions.9: Taste and add salt if necessary.

w-mx-042.culturalNotes: Picadillo is a popular dish in Mexico, often served with rice or tortillas.

w-mx-043.title: Mexican Pozole Roja

instructions.1: In a large pot, add 2 cups of water and the drained hominy.
instructions.2: In a separate large pot, place the chicken pieces and add enough water to cover by a couple inches. Add the onion, cilantro, and 1 tablespoon of salt.
instructions.3: Bring to a boil then reduce heat to a simmer over medium low and cover. Cook for about 45 minutes until the chicken is cooked and tender. Remove the chicken pieces from the pot, strain and reserve the cooking liquid.
instructions.4: When the chicken is cool enough to handle, remove and discard the skin and bones and shred the meat.
instructions.5: Put the chicken and the reserved liquid into the pot with hominy. Place the pot over medium heat until warm. Add salt if needed.
instructions.6: For the red sauce: Place the chilies in a medium saucepan, add just enough water to cover and bring to a boil. Reduce to simmer and until the chilies are soft, about 10 minutes or so.
instructions.7: Put the chilies and 3/4 cup of the soaking liquid into a blender along with the onion, garlic, cloves, cumin, and salt. Blend until smooth.
instructions.8: Run this through a fine mesh sieve into a bowl, using a spoon to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard what does not go through.
instructions.9: Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan over medium high heat until it comes to a simmer, add in the chili liquid and bring to a boil then reduce to simmer, stirring occasionally. The sauce will thicken cook in total about 5 or 6 minutes and remove from heat.
instructions.10: Assuming your pozole is still warm turn up the temperature to medium high. Stir in the chili mixture and add salt to taste.
instructions.11: Serve the pozole hot with the accompaniments listed above. Make sure to squeeze lime over the soup, it makes the dish complete.

w-mx-043.culturalNotes: Pozole is a traditional Mexican dish served on special occasions and celebrations. It is known for its rich and spicy flavors.

w-mx-044.title: Rajas con Crema

instructions.1: Grill the poblanos over medium heat until charred all over, for about 20-30 minutes, turning the peppers every 10 minutes.
instructions.2: When done, place the peppers on a platter and cover with a bowl or plastic wrap for 5-10 minutes to steam the skins loose.
instructions.3: Peel the poblanos and discard the skins, then slice them into bite-sized strips.
instructions.4: Grate the cheese.
instructions.5: Cook the onion in a large pan until softened.
instructions.6: Add the poblanos, cheese, and crema mexicana to the onion.
instructions.7: You may also add corn as well as any salt or pepper, as desired. Heat through.

w-mx-044.culturalNotes: Rajas con Crema is a traditional Mexican dish served as an appetizer or part of a main meal.

w-mx-046.title: Chile Relleno

w-mx-046-i2.name: Monterey Jack cheese
w-mx-046-i2.standardAmount: 8 ounces (cut into long strips or shredded)

instructions.1: Roast the poblano peppers over medium heat until the skin is blackened. Place them in a sealed plastic bag for 10 minutes to cool.
instructions.2: Peel the peppers and cut off the stem. Gently open the peppers and remove the seeds and inner membrane.
instructions.3: Stuff the peppers with Monterey Jack cheese. Set the stuffed peppers aside.
instructions.4: In a bowl, beat the eggs with salt. In another bowl, place the flour.
instructions.5: Dip the stuffed peppers in the flour, then in the beaten eggs.
instructions.6: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Fry the peppers until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.7: Make the tomato sauce by blending the tomatoes, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cilantro, salt, and olive oil in a blender until smooth.
instructions.8: Serve the stuffed peppers with the tomato sauce on the side.

w-mx-046.culturalNotes: Chile relleno is a traditional Mexican dish often served on special occasions.

w-mx-048.title: Mexican Cinnamon Tea

instructions.1: Place the water and cinnamon in a medium-sized saucepan and bring to a boil.
instructions.2: Let it boil for 3-5 minutes, then remove from heat.
instructions.3: Let it steep for an additional 30 minutes or to taste based on desired strength.
instructions.4: Add honey to taste.
instructions.5: Serve warm.

w-mx-048.culturalNotes: Mexican cinnamon tea is a traditional drink that is very popular in Mexico, especially during holidays and special occasions.

w-mx-049.title: Fish Fillet with Garlic Sauce

w-mx-049-i4.name: Vegetable oil (or a mix of half olive oil and half vegetable oil)

instructions.1: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Set aside while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over low heat. Once hot, fry the garlic slices until they are golden. Make sure to remove them promptly once they are lightly golden; if you leave them longer, they will get a bitter taste.
instructions.3: If using the flour, dust the fillets with the flour lightly. Then, turn the heat to medium-high on the frying pan where you cooked the garlic. Once hot, add the fish and cook on both sides. The cooking time will depend on the fish’s thickness. It will be about 2-3 minutes per side for those fillets about 1/3 inch thick, and about 5-7 minutes for thicker fillets.
instructions.4: Remove the fish from the frying pan and place it on a cooling rack with paper towel underneath to absorb any excess fat.
instructions.5: Serve the fish garnished with the chopped parsley and golden garlic slices. (And if you add a little dab of butter, oh heavens!)

w-mx-049.culturalNotes: This dish is one of the popular dishes in Mexican cuisine, often served as a main course at family gatherings.

w-mx-050.title: Green Chile and Cheese Quesadilla

instructions.1: Preheat a comal for 1 minute over medium-low heat.
instructions.2: Warm tortillas for 1 minute on one side, flip and sprinkle some of the cheese on one of the tortillas, add chile, and top with another tortilla and press gently with a spatula.
instructions.3: Flip occasionally until quesadillas are golden brown on each side and cheese has melted.
instructions.4: Repeat with remaining tortillas and ingredients.
instructions.5: Top them with salsa and guacamole, if desired.

w-mx-050.culturalNotes: Quesadilla is a popular dish in Mexico, served as a snack or main meal.
